name: The Haçienda (site)
places: Site of the Haçienda club, Whitworth Street West
description: The site of the Haçienda nightclub (1982–97), the centre of the city’s acid house scene. The building that replaced it is flats named after it.

name: Free Trade Hall
description: A Victorian hall on the site of the Peterloo Massacre, for a century the city’s main concert hall. It is now a hotel.

name: Old Trafford
description: Manchester United’s home stadium, just outside the city centre, with a club museum and stadium tours.

name: Manchester Central Library
description: The city’s main public library, a round domed building from the 1930s on St Peter’s Square, with a large reading room under the dome.

name: Chetham’s Library
description: A public library founded in 1653 in a medieval building near the cathedral, often called the oldest in the English-speaking world.

name: Pankhurst Centre
description: The house where Emmeline Pankhurst founded the Women’s Social and Political Union in 1903, now a small museum and women’s centre.

name: Salford Lads Club
description: A youth club opened in 1903 that is still running. Fans of The Smiths come to photograph the doorway seen in the band’s 1986 album artwork.

name: St Peter’s Square
description: A city-centre square on part of the site of the 1819 Peterloo Massacre, when cavalry charged a peaceful crowd calling for the vote.

name: Manchester Town Hall
description: The Victorian Gothic town hall on Albert Square, finished in 1877, with murals of the city’s history in the Great Hall.
